items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah, I guess Andy Edwards had left. I think, though. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, well, he left, let's see, oh, I think about two years after I went to the Palace Theater.

ctx.x: But, uh, we used to, uh, bounty-hoo on Dauphin Street. So, Joe Fulco called me on the side. He says, hey boy, I had to give you a job. I said, what? He says, to play vaudeville. I said, well, I'm not that good. I said, you know, I can't read music that good to play vaudeville, see? He says, I'll teach you. Yeah, well, Sidney Wilson, I don't know if you know the piano player Sidney Wilson? No, I don't know him. He was a trombone player too. Leo Brookhoven, Trappertone. So those two guys really helped me, you know,…
Yeah, I guess Andy Edwards had left. I think, though.
Yeah, well, he left, let's see, oh, I think about two years after I went to the Palace Theater.
